=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clearly visible paired leaves attached at the same node along the stem in all images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced out along the stem, not clustered at the tips)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (leaves are undivided blades attached directly to the stem)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (smooth edge with no teeth or serrations visible)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): ovate to elliptic (broadest in the middle, tapering towards base and apex)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (tapering to a distinct, elongated point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded to broadly cuneate (base is generally rounded, occasionally slightly tapering)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with veins branching off laterally)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, moderately spaced, branching from the midrib
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): glabrous and shiny (surface appears smooth, hairless, and reflective)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no hairs visible on the leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles appear relatively short compared to the leaf blade length)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear cylindrical and round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears rigid, brownish-green, and lignified)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem surface appears smooth without visible hairs)
    19. Stem color: green to brownish-green (stem exhibits a mix of green and brown tones, with some lichen or algae growth)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (stem surface appears relatively smooth, lacking prominent ridges or large lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the leaf bases in any of the images)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex exudate is visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus structure is visible at the petiole base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are visible)
F. Notes: Several leaves show white, winding trails on their surface, indicating damage likely from leaf-mining larvae. Some leaves also have small holes and missing margin sections. The plant is growing in a forest floor environment with leaf litter and other vegetation.
